title: Make jelly worth reaching for
goal: Check this app is it useful for you

steps.title: Try jelly as an agent
steps.why: Is it useful to the agent it is built for?

result.text: Useful: made a jelly, asked, looked and undid in seconds. Eight rough edges.

show.after:
$ jelly new plan --view view.html --verbs verbs.js --state state.json --about "trial"
trial:plan v1: made
$ jelly call plan add '{"title":"second"}'
trial:plan v2: add ran · changed /items
$ jelly call plan add '{}'
jelly: title needed
$ jelly undo plan
trial:plan v5: undo · changed /items

notes.text: Check this app is it useful for you

steps.title: Log what would make it better

result.text: Eight outcome-driven issues, #1 to #8, each with evidence and a done-when list.

show.after:
#1  An agent can ask a question and get the answer in one command
#2  jelly wait never misses a change made before it started listening
#3  Every agent in a project sees everything the person did
#4  jelly is running whenever an agent reaches for it
#5  jelly ask says so when its --at matches nothing
#6  The first jelly see after the daemon starts returns a snapshot
#7  Every command an agent reads prints one line per item
#8  Only jelly's own pages and the CLI can talk to the daemon

steps.title: Review recipe, first cut
steps.why: Outcomes with evidence, changes by intent, approve or push back.

result.text: Worked end to end, and read as prose in boxes. Commit cc1498b.

show.caption: Every verb, refusal and the inbox checked on a throwaway daemon.

notes.text: It’s not very visual at all and still a wall of text

result.text: A map, before and after, one change at a time. Commit 15569be.

show.caption: Clicked through in a real browser: push back, pick on the map, approve, arrow keys. No page errors.

steps.title: Fix issue #5 for real
steps.why: A real change to review, instead of an invented one.

result.text: jelly ask and jelly look now say when --at matches nothing. About 0.7 s per ask. Commit ef60c62.

show.before:
$ jelly ask plan "Which order?" --at "#nope"
it shows on the page below #nope
show.after:
$ jelly ask plan "Which order?" --at "#nope"
#nope matches nothing on the page, so it shows at the top
show.caption: The page has no #nope.

steps.title: Review the fix in the recipe

result.text: All 104 changed lines sit in five changes; the recipe's example is now this review. Commit d37025b.

gate.note: The review ends on Go, and that is yours to say.

steps.title: Build more recipes
steps.why: Starting points for the jellies that are easy to get wrong the first time.

progress.text: Four at once: plan, triage, map and monitor.

show.after:
$ ls skill/recipes
map  monitor  plan  review  triage

notes.text: Build some more recipes. This tool is for you, don’t limit yourself.

steps.title: Log bugs found along the way
steps.why: New issues, or evidence on the ones that exist.

notes.text: Log bugs as well when and if you find them or add evidence to existing
Two so far: headless Chrome posts its snapshot and then lingers (evidence for #6), and jelly share drops images named in state.

steps.title: List every recipe in the skill
steps.why: One line each in SKILL.md, so a session reads a recipe only when it uses it.
